messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Multiple TLS handshake failures observed for prod inference endpoints in us-west-2 (auto-page to on-call)

alex.m: I'm on it, paging went to both SRE and Network. What are we seeing for customer impact? any 5xx spike in hosted API?

priya: started seeing errors at ~07:32 UTC. Grafana shows a spike in 524/502s for /v1/generate from a handful of clusters in us-west-2. CC @sam.network

sam.network: I'm looking at tcpdump from the egress NATgw in the us-west-2-azb region. seeing a wall of retransmits and a bunch of TLS ClientHellos that never complete. Example (client -> model-proxy 10.0.44.12:443):

```
16:07:34.123456 IP 10.1.5.22.45678 > 10.0.44.12:443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1452,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
16:07:34.123789 IP 10.1.5.22.45678 > 10.0.44.12:443: Flags [P.], seq 12346:12639, ack 1, win 64240
... retransmit ...
```

maria.sre: kubectl logs from envoy sidecar in the model pod show a lot of `SSL_read: Connection reset by peer` and `handshake did not complete` errors. Example:

```
[warning] TLS handshake failed: SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:wrong version number
[error] SSL_read failed: ECONNRESET (104)
```

chris.cs: customers are reporting timeouts, some are getting 502s. We should surface hit list: high-throughput customers and any VIP contract customers. Triage priority-high.

alex.m: Hypotheses:
- cert rotation issue (recent rotation job ran at 07:30) -> broken cert chain
- VPC peering/route change causing MTU/path fragmentation issues -> ClientHello too large
- Upstream load balancer/envoy config drift (ALPN/TLS1.3 incompat)

priya: note: cert-rotation job executed at 07:31 across many nodes. I rolled back rotation on a test node and ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.44.12:443 -servername api.prod.redwood`:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...: SSL handshake failure
139724...: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 294 bytes
```

sam.network: interesting — but tcpdump suggests a lot of retransmits and MSS 1452. I tried an s_client from inside the same AZ -> handshake completes. From cross-AZ it fails. That points at path MTU/peering. Also saw ICMP need-to-frag messages suppressed somewhere.

maria.sre: also, envoy logs show `TLSv1.3 handshake aborted: received unexpected EOF`. If MTU were dropping fragments, you'd expect incomplete ClientHello. The ClientHello can be large with multiple extensions (SNI, ALPN, key share). That aligns.

alex.m: Let's split work: Sam + Network team validate MTU/peering path. Priya + SRE validate cert chain and envoy configs. I'll coordinate mitigations and customer comms.

sam.network: I ran `traceroute -F` and `ip mtu` checks. On the VPC peering path between us-west-2-vpcA and vpcB the MTU on one of the transit hops is set to 1400 due to a recent infra change (VPN appliance health update). Some of our NATGW setups still assume 1500; fragmentation gets dropped. Found iptables `CLAMP_MSS` removed on a new NAT build.

```
# on natgw-2
ip link show
2: eth0: mtu 1400 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000

# on natgw-1 (old)
eth0 mtu 1500
```

priya: for certs: the rotation job used an intermediate chain that a few older clients might not trust, but majority of handshakes failing are cross-AZ only. I don't think certs are the primary cause, but we should still verify chain on rotated certs. Repo: `infra/certs/rotation/2026-03-15`.

maria.sre: mitigation attempt 1: enabling `proxy_protocol` fallback route and increasing envoy handshake timeout from 5s -> 12s showed slight reduction in errors for same-AZ traffic but cross-AZ still failing. That supports network MTU hypothesis.

alex.m: Immediate mitigation options:
- Hotfix A: rollback NATGW build to restore CLAMP_MSS and MTU 1500 where possible (Network)
- Hotfix B: route critical customer traffic via a known-good path (bypass peering) -> add route table entry (Network)
- Hotfix C: temporarily enable smaller TLS records / configure envoy to send smaller ClientHello? (applicable? low confidence)

sam.network: I'm pushing a rollback for the new NAT build on natgw-2 in us-west-2-azb now. Also adding CLAMP_MSS via iptables `--clamp-mss-to-pmtu` as an emergency stopgap.

```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: natgw-2 -> previous image `natgw:2026-03-02` (rollback ticket #INC-3829).

sam.network: Rollback applied, CLAMP_MSS added. Running tcpdump... retransmits dropped by ~90%, handshake success rate increased to ~95% in affected az.

maria.sre: confirmed via logs: envoy handshake exceptions dropped off. Grafana shows error rate returning to baseline for /v1/generate. P95 latency improving.

chris.cs: communicating to customers: sent initial note to VIPs with ETA ~30m. Will follow up postmortem and RCA.

alex.m: Triage summary so far: primary cause = MTU mismatch introduced by recent NATGW build/policy, which caused TLS ClientHello fragmentation and handshake failures cross-AZ. Secondary possible contributor = cert rotation introduced at same window but not primary (evidence: same-AZ succeeded; cert rollback in test didn't change cross-AZ failures).

priya: assigned owners for RCA artifacts:
- sam.network -> root cause writeup (network path, NAT build change, config diff)
- maria.sre -> timeline + logs collection (envoy, tcpdump, kube events)
- priya -> cert rotation verification & mitigation notes
- alex.m -> customer impact summary and incident timeline

maria.sre: attaching key logs in thread:

```
kubectl -n inference logs model-server-abc envoy | grep -i handshake | tail -n 50
# tcpdump snippet saved to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1902456789/tcpdump.pcap
openssl s_client -connect 34.201.66.12:443 -servername api.prod.redwood -msg
```

sam.network: Follow-ups:
- rollback NATGW images for the remaining updated nodes in us-west-2 (in progress)
- enable CLAMP_MSS at NAT layer for all peered routes as precaution
- add a path-MTU monitor to our infra tests (alert on MTU < 1500 on critical peering)

priya: Cert follow-ups:
- verify rotated cert chain is complete & rebuild rotation job test harness to catch chain mismatches.
- add cert rotation smoke test that does cross-AZ s_client checks from a synthetic client.

alex.m: Postmortem owners OK. We'll keep this thread as the working log. I'll open a formal postmortem doc and link it here. Immediate note: incident declared resolved at 08:05 UTC after NATGW rollback and CLAMP_MSS fix; last_message_ts will be updated once postmortem link is ready.

chris.cs: great job team. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and give ops clearance to close customer-facing communications after the RCA is published.

maria.sre: tentative RCA doc link (WIP): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3829-RCA (I'll paste final doc once done)

alex.m: closing timeline: start 07:32 UTC, mitigations applied 07:46 UTC, resolved 08:05 UTC. Adding post-incident actions to ops board. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-bot: alert auto-closure scheduled in 72h unless postmortem filed.

sam.network: adding final note: root cause = NATGW image upgrade removed CLAMP_MSS and lowered MTU on eth0 to 1400 for traffic transiting a peering hop; result was fragment drop causing incomplete TLS handshakes for larger ClientHello messages across AZs. Fix = rollback + re-add CLAMP_MSS + test harness. Will include diffs in RCA.

maria.sre: I'll upload the tcpdump excerpt and envoy log extract to the incident S3 folder shortly.

alex.m: thanks everyone. Incident thread will remain open until PM posts the final RCA and customer comms are complete.
